extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO, OED staff, and persons subject to USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for approving an Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and the consequences of consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) for Affidavit of Resignation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order determined that Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation "complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)." The body of the affidavit is used to show compliance by reciting key elements (see separate entries for the affidavit's enumerated acknowledgments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Freely and voluntarily rendered consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must state that the respondent's consent is freely and voluntarily rendered and that the respondent is not being subjected to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact wording from the affidavit: "His consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress." This is a required element for acceptance of a consent exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending disciplinary complaint and factual allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge awareness that a disciplinary complaint is pending and set forth the factual allegations (e.g., licensure, prior proceedings, activities leading to investigation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit here explicitly lists awareness of: a pending complaint before an Administrative Law Judge (USPTO Proceeding No. D2018-45); prior OED filings (e.g., D2016-20); a prior exclusion (January 26, 2017); the creation of TTC Business Solutions; filing and preparing thousands of trademark applications; and the opening of multiple OED investigations (file numbers 03073, 03110, 03197, 03241). The affidavit's recitation of alleged facts demonstrates the respondent's awareness of the allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of alleged violations of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit should identify which provisions of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct are alleged to have been violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists the alleged rule violations as: 37 C.F.R. § 503 (responsibilities regarding non-practitioner assistants); 37 C.F.R. § 505 (practicing law before the USPTO in violation of USPTO regulations or assisting another in doing so); 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) (conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation); 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) (conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice); and 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i) (other conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice). The affidavit may elect not to admit the violations but must acknowledge the allegations for purposes of the consent exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of legal and factual consequences and relevant regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent must state that he has fully read and understands the pertinent regulations and the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit here states: "He has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(6), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60, and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO in trademark and non-patent matters." This demonstrates the required informed consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to be excluded from practice before the USPTO in trademark and non-patent matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must include an explicit consent to be excluded from practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the affidavit states: "He consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in trademark and non-patent matters." The Final Order then approves the affidavit and orders exclusion on consent effective the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on excluded practitioners and definition of practice (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58(a), 11.5(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded practitioner may not engage in practice before the USPTO in trademark matters; 'practice' includes consulting with or giving advice to a client in contemplation of filing a trademark application or other documents with the USPTO and preparing such applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites: "An excluded practitioner may not engage in the practice of trademark law before the Office. See 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(a)." and that "Practice before the USPTO in trademark matters includes, but is not limited to, consulting with or giving advice to a client in contemplation of filing a trademark application or other document with the USPTO. See 37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b)(2)." The Order uses TTC Business Solutions' activities (consulting/advice and preparing trademark applications) as examples of prohibited conduct by an excluded practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED investigative authority and practitioner's obligation to respond to RFIs (37 C.F.R. § 11.22(f)(1)(ii); § 11.801(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: During an investigation the OED Director may request information and evidence; a practitioner has an ethical obligation to respond to any lawfully issued Request for Information (RFI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites: "During the course of an investigation, the OED Director may request from a practitioner information and evidence regarding possible grounds for discipline... See 37 C.F.R. § 11.22(f)(1)(ii)." and "A practitioner has an ethical obligation to respond to any lawfully issued RFI. See 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b)." The respondent here was found to have been provided ample notice and opportunity but failed to respond to multiple RFIs in the identified OED files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions applicable to reinstatement applications under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: By consenting to exclusion, the respondent acknowledges that, if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume for the limited purpose of determining reinstatement that the allegations are true and that the respondent could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit contains the acknowledgment: (a) the allegations regarding him in Proceeding No. D2018-45 are true, and (b) he could not have successfully defended himself against the allegations. The Order reiterates this presumption as a consequence of consenting to exclusion and as binding for reinstatement consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and Official Gazette notice requirements upon approval of consent exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the specified notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order mandates: (i) electronic publication of the Final Order at https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/ and (ii) that the OED Director publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided "Notice of Exclusion on Consent" text, which summarizes the facts, alleged violations, prior exclusions, and reinstatement presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-approval obligations and case disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon approval of the Affidavit of Resignation, the respondent must comply with relevant regulations (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and § 11.60 upon any reinstatement request) and the underlying disciplinary proceeding is dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly orders: "Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; and Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement; and USPTO Disciplinary Proceeding No. D2018-45 is hereby dismissed." These are the continuing conditions and procedural disposition resulting from approval of the affidavit.
